**R373** (Section 15.5.2, MAY): The user agent MAY repeat the request with a new or replaced Authorization header field (Section 11.6.2).

**R374** (Section 15.5.2, SHOULD): If the 401 response contains the same challenge as the prior response, and the user agent has already attempted authentication at least once, then the user agent SHOULD present the enclosed representation to the user, since it usually contains relevant diagnostic information.

**R375** (Section 15.5.4, SHOULD): The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials.

**R376** (Section 15.5.4, MAY): The client MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials.

**R377** (Section 15.5.4, MAY): An origin server that wishes to "hide" the current existence of a forbidden target resource MAY instead respond with a status code of 404 (Not Found).

**R378** (Section 15.5.6, MUST): The origin server MUST generate an Allow header field in a 405 response containing a list of the target resource's currently supported methods.

**R379** (Section 15.5.7, SHOULD): The server SHOULD generate content containing a list of available representation characteristics and corresponding resource identifiers from which the user or user agent can choose the one most appropriate.

**R380** (Section 15.5.7, MAY): A user agent MAY automatically select the most appropriate choice from that list.

**R381** (Section 15.5.8, MUST): The proxy MUST send a Proxy-Authenticate header field (Section 11.7.1) containing a challenge applicable to that proxy for the request.

**R382** (Section 15.5.8, MAY): The client MAY repeat the request with a new or replaced Proxy-Authorization header field (Section 11.7.2).

**R383** (Section 15.5.9, MAY): If the client has an outstanding request in transit, it MAY repeat that request.

**R384** (Section 15.5.10, SHOULD): The server SHOULD generate content that includes enough information for a user to recognize the source of the conflict.

**R385** (Section 15.5.12, MAY): The client MAY repeat the request if it adds a valid Content-Length header field containing the length of the request content.

**R386** (Section 15.5.14, MAY): The server MAY terminate the request, if the protocol version in use allows it; otherwise, the server MAY close the connection.

**R387** (Section 15.5.14, SHOULD): If the condition is temporary, the server SHOULD generate a Retry-After header field to indicate that it is temporary and after what time the client MAY try again.

**R388** (Section 15.5.17, SHOULD): A server that generates a 416 response to a byte-range request SHOULD generate a Content-Range header field specifying the current length of the selected representation (Section 14.4).

**R389** (Section 15.5.20, MAY): A client that receives a 421 (Misdirected Request) response MAY retry the request, whether or not the request method is idempotent, over a different connection, such as a fresh connection specific to the target resource's origin, or via an alternative service [ALTSVC].

**R390** (Section 15.5.20, MUST): A proxy MUST NOT generate a 421 response.

**R391** (Section 15.5.22, MUST): The server MUST send an Upgrade header field in a 426 response to indicate the required protocol(s) (Section 7.8).

**R392** (Section 15.6, SHOULD): Except when responding to a HEAD request, the server SHOULD send a representation containing an explanation of the error situation, and whether it is a temporary or permanent condition.

**R393** (Section 15.6, SHOULD): A user agent SHOULD display any included representation to the user.

**R394** (Section 15.6.4, MAY): The server MAY send a Retry-After header field (Section 10.2.3) to suggest an appropriate amount of time for the client to wait before retrying the request.

**R395** (Section 15.6.6, SHOULD): The server SHOULD generate a representation for the 505 response that describes why that version is not supported and what other protocols are supported by that server.

**R396** (Section 16.1.1, MUST): HTTP method registrations MUST include the following fields:

**R397** (Section 16.2.1, MUST): A registration MUST include the following fields:

**R398** (Section 16.3.1, MUST): It MUST conform to the field-name syntax defined in Section 5.1, and it SHOULD be restricted to just letters, digits, and hyphen ('-') characters, with the first character being a letter.

**R399** (Section 16.3.2.1, SHOULD): To be interoperable, new field names SHOULD constrain themselves to alphanumeric characters, "-", and ".", and SHOULD begin with a letter.

**R400** (Section 16.4.1, MUST): Registrations MUST include the following fields:

**R401** (Section 16.4.2, MUST): * HTTP authentication is presumed to be stateless: all of the information necessary to authenticate a request MUST be provided in the request, rather than be dependent on the server remembering prior requests.

**R402** (Section 16.4.2, MUST): New schemes MUST NOT use it in a way incompatible with that definition.

**R403** (Section 16.5.1, MUST): Registration of an HTTP Range Unit MUST include the following fields:

**R404** (Section 16.6.1, MUST): Content coding registrations MUST include the following fields:

**R405** (Section 16.6.1, MUST): Names of content codings MUST NOT overlap with names of transfer codings (per the "HTTP Transfer Coding Registry" located at <https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-parameters/>) unless the encoding transformation is identical (as is the case for the compression codings defined in Section 8.4.1).

**R406** (Section 16.6.1, MUST): Values to be added to this namespace require IETF Review (see Section 4.8 of [RFC8126]) and MUST conform to the purpose of content coding defined in Section 8.4.1.

**R407** (Section 16.7, MUST): The registration MUST name a responsible party for the registration.

**R408** (Section 16.7, MUST): The registration MUST name a point of contact.

**R409** (Section 16.7, MAY): The registration MAY name a set of specifications associated with that token.

**R410** (Section 16.7, SHOULD): The registration SHOULD name a set of expected "protocol-version" tokens associated with that token at the time of registration.

**R411** (Section 16.7, MAY): The responsible party MAY change the registration at any time.

**R412** (Section 16.7, MAY): The IESG MAY reassign responsibility for a protocol token.
